name: Design & UI Quality
when_applicable: Projects with user-facing interfaces (web, mobile, desktop applications)
verification: Follow ui_verification: browser_snapshot YAML for roles/names/text/URL/state; bounding box or CDP getComputedStyle for size/contrast/overflow; screenshot only if paint/overlap cannot be falsified that way. No Playwright unless the user asks.

criteria.criterion: All interactive elements are keyboard-accessible — focusable, activatable, and navigable without a mouse
criteria.how_to_test: Tab or click through controls. After each move, browser_snapshot: every button/link/input has a role and is reachable. Flag custom widgets without tabIndex/keyboard handler. Do not screenshot.

criteria.criterion: Interactive elements have accessible names — via visible labels, aria-label, or aria-labelledby
criteria.how_to_test: Check buttons, inputs, and icons for accessible names. Flag icon-only buttons without aria-label, inputs without labels.

criteria.criterion: Text meets WCAG AA contrast ratios — 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text
criteria.how_to_test: CDP getComputedStyle color vs background; compute WCAG ratio. Flag below 4.5:1 (normal) or 3:1 (large). Screenshot only if text sits on image/gradient (snapshot/CDP cannot falsify).

criteria.criterion: Information is not conveyed by color alone — additional indicators (icons, text, patterns) supplement color
criteria.how_to_test: Check error states, status indicators, charts. If removing color makes information ambiguous, flag it.

criteria.criterion: Focus indicators are visible and clear — custom focus styles exist and are not suppressed with outline:none without replacement
criteria.how_to_test: Tab to each control. CDP getComputedStyle for outline/box-shadow (flag outline:none without replacement). Snapshot confirms which control is focused. Screenshot only if the ring is paint-only.

criteria.criterion: Semantic HTML is used — proper heading hierarchy (h1-h6), landmarks (nav, main, aside), lists, and form elements
criteria.how_to_test: Check for div/span used where semantic elements belong. Flag clickable divs without role='button', non-hierarchical headings.

criteria.criterion: Spacing uses a consistent scale (4px or 8px base) — no arbitrary pixel values scattered through the codebase
criteria.how_to_test: Search for padding/margin values. Flag raw pixel values that don't align with the spacing scale (e.g., 7px, 13px, 22px).

criteria.criterion: Colors come from a defined palette/token system — no hardcoded hex values outside the token definitions
criteria.how_to_test: Search for raw hex colors (#xxx) or rgb() outside of theme/token files. Flag inline color values in components.

criteria.criterion: Typography uses a defined scale — limited set of font sizes, weights, and line heights from tokens, not arbitrary values
criteria.how_to_test: Search for font-size declarations. Flag values outside the type scale. Check for consistent line-height ratios.

criteria.criterion: Each screen has a clear focal point — one primary action, clear heading structure, obvious reading flow
criteria.how_to_test: browser_snapshot: one clear heading and one primary button name. Flag 3+ competing primary buttons or missing heading. Do not screenshot.

criteria.criterion: Complex interfaces use progressive disclosure — only essential info shown upfront, details available on demand
criteria.how_to_test: browser_snapshot of the initial view. Flag 10+ visible inputs or no grouping (headings/landmarks). Do not screenshot.

criteria.criterion: Layout adapts to mobile (320px+), tablet (768px+), and desktop (1024px+) without horizontal scrolling or broken elements
criteria.how_to_test: Resize to 320, 768, and 1024. At each width: browser_snapshot for truncated/missing roles; bounding box or scrollWidth>clientWidth for overflow/overlap. Screenshot only if overlap is paint-only.

criteria.criterion: Touch targets are minimum 44x44px on mobile — buttons, links, and interactive areas are large enough to tap
criteria.how_to_test: At mobile viewport, browser_get_bounding_box (or getBoundingClientRect) on interactive elements. Flag width or height below 44px. Do not screenshot.

criteria.criterion: Every user action provides immediate feedback — loading states, success confirmations, error messages
criteria.how_to_test: Trigger the action. Re-snapshot: loading/status/alert/text appeared. Flag silent actions. Do not screenshot.

criteria.criterion: Error messages are helpful and actionable — they explain what went wrong and how to fix it, not just 'Error occurred'
criteria.how_to_test: Trigger invalid input or failure. Re-snapshot: specific error text (not generic 'Something went wrong'). Do not screenshot.

criteria.criterion: Interactive elements have clear states — default, hover, active, disabled, loading. Users can tell what's clickable.
criteria.how_to_test: Snapshot for disabled/aria-busy/aria-disabled. Hover/active: CDP getComputedStyle. Screenshot only if hover paint cannot be read from CSS.

criteria.criterion: Similar components have consistent APIs — same prop naming (variant, size, disabled), same patterns across the system
criteria.how_to_test: Compare prop interfaces across related components (Button, Input, Select). Flag inconsistent naming (size vs sz, isDisabled vs disabled).

criteria.criterion: Components are composable — compound components over monolithic configs (Card + CardHeader + CardBody over Card with 15 props)
criteria.how_to_test: Check component APIs. Flag components with 10+ props that could be split into composable sub-components.

criteria.criterion: Visual rhythm is consistent — same spacing between similar elements, aligned grids, no arbitrary one-off spacings
criteria.how_to_test: CDP getComputedStyle margin/gap/padding on repeated elements (cards, list items, fields). Flag inconsistent gaps in the same context. Do not screenshot.

criteria.criterion: Similar UI patterns use the same solution — not 3 different modal implementations or 2 different form patterns
criteria.how_to_test: Find repeated patterns (modals, forms, tables, notifications). Check if they use the same component/approach. Flag divergent implementations.
